chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Or two others from those other than you' (1). He said: 'If a man is in a foreign land and no Muslim is found there, the testimony of a non-Muslim is valid regarding the will (testament).'
ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of non-Muslims valid for a will in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the exception to the general rule of requiring Muslim witnesses for wills, specifically addressing the practical necessity in diaspora contexts. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of *al-maslahah* (public interest) and *darurah* (necessity), allowing non-Muslim testimony when no Muslim witnesses are available to ensure the deceased's wishes are honored. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in adapting legal requirements to geographical and demographic realities.
